name: battery-display
title: Battery Percentage
summary: Shows a battery percentage beside the icon.
description: Shows the battery as an icon, as a percentage, or as both. It can also use the curve of a 3000 mAh battery or a curve from your own battery in place of the Apple table.
details: During a charge, the iPod shows the charge icon and the percentage. With Display set to Icon, it shows only the charge icon.
The Apple data moves in steps of 5 %. The Apple icon has only 16 levels.
3000 mAh and Custom change the battery picture and the percentage. They do not change when the iPod stops.
Battery Curve imports a battery log, so that you can make a curve for your own battery. Custom uses this curve.
Without an imported log, Custom uses the 3000 mAh curve.
After a start, the percentage shows when the first value is ready. Until then, the iPod shows the icon.
notes: The 3000 mAh curve comes from one battery. Other batteries are different. Import a log for your own battery.
The percentage reads high during a charge, because the charge raises the voltage.
The layout is tested only in the emulator. Check the text and the title on each screen of the iPod.

choices.title: Icon + Percent
choices.description: The battery icon, and the percentage at its left.
choices.caution: This is not tested. The text can touch a long title.

choices.title: Apple
choices.description: The Apple table. Use this for a battery of the original size.

choices.title: 3000 mAh
choices.description: The curve of a 3000 mAh battery. It changes the icon and the percentage.
choices.caution: The curve is from one battery. Other batteries are different.

choices.title: Custom
choices.description: The curve from your battery log in Battery Curve. It changes the icon and the percentage.
choices.caution: Without an imported log, this choice uses the 3000 mAh curve.

choices.title: Off
choices.description: The percentage follows the data directly. Apple data moves in steps of 5 %.

choices.title: On
choices.description: A longer average, and no small rises. Apple data moves in steps of 1 %, but it is then not the exact Apple logic. The value changes more slowly, and it can stay still for some minutes.
